title: Avoid Using Sanitary Tees Horizontally
description: Using a sanitary tee on its back or side for a horizontal drainage connection is a common installation mistake that causes frequent pipe blockages. A sanitary tee features a short radius turn designed for vertical-to-horizontal or horizontal-to-vertical transitions where gravity assists waste flow. When placed horizontally, solid waste loses velocity and accumulates inside the branch inlet, gradually choking the pipe. For horizontal-to-horizontal drainage branches, plumbing codes require a combination wye and 1/8 bend or a long-sweep fitting. Using directional fittings with a wide radius ensures smooth waste flow and maintains proper self-scouring velocity throughout the DWV system.

Using directional fittings with a wide radius ensures smooth waste flow and maintains proper self-scouring velocity throughout the DWV system.
